title: Show tool calls on their own rows instead of folding runs of them into one summary
description:
The main screen folds runs of tool calls into one summary line. With this patch they show as ordinary rows with their results — reads, searches and directory listings (including the read-only shell commands behind them), MCP calls, memory / workshop / scratchpad writes, REPL, and in fullscreen ToolSearch and other shell commands.

Kept folding: the todo and task tools (TodoWrite, TaskCreate, TaskGet, TaskUpdate, TaskList). Upstream absorbs them silently — there is nothing in their rows worth reading — and pops one out only when it fails. Also left as upstream has them: thinking folds into its own 'Thought for Xs' line, and PreToolUse hook summaries and recalled memories are absorbed into whatever group is open when they arrive.

The fold is a grouping pass over the message list, and a group's summary line is the only place the main screen shows thinking — a raw thinking block renders nothing outside Ctrl+O or verbose mode. So the grouping pass itself is not touched; tool calls are just refused admission to it, each becoming a break point.

sites.description:
The function the grouping pass asks whether a tool call may join a fold. It is the only point in the chain used for nothing but grouping: the classifier behind it is exported and also feeds the renderer and the recent-activity display, so changing the classifier would reach those too. This one is called only by the grouping pass's per-message cache.

Identified as the two-parameter function that handles grouped_tool_use and returns the fold record — toolUseIds, readPaths, isAbsorbedSilently among its fields.

`if(!<classification>) return null` — where the function already turns away tools the classifier does not fold. Widened to turn away everything except the todo/task tools.

Those are told apart by popsOutOnError, which the classifier sets true for exactly that list and nothing else: ToolSearch shares the silent-absorb branch but gets false, and REPL does not carry the field. Testing the flag rather than tool names keeps the list where upstream maintains it.

verify.describe: only the todo/task tools are still admitted to a fold
